record.title: The majority out-dominating number conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{r,s}$ be a complete bipartite graph with $r\leq s$, and let $DOM^{+}_m(K_{r,s})$ denote its majority out-dominating number. Assume that $DOM^{+}_m(K_{r,s})\neq1$. 

**Majority out-dominating number conjecture.**

$$
DOM^{+}_m(K_{r,s}) = \begin{cases} 2 & \text{if } s\leq r+2,\\ \left\lceil\frac{s-r}{2}\right\rceil & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

The preceding results determine exactly when this parameter equals $1$, but the general value for complete bipartite graphs is described as difficult to find. The displayed formula is proposed as the conjectured value in all remaining cases; its resolution is not indicated in the source.
record.source_name: Karam Ebadi, Martín Manrique, Reza Jafary and J. Joseline Manora, “Majority out-dominating sets in digraphs”, arXiv:1311.0479 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.0479

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).
